title: Hybrid shard-probe top-k with offset-based resumable pages for reranker
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Customers want predictable, low-latency reranking responses for high-volume candidate sets while still being able to page through large result sets. Current naive top_k semantics return either a global top-k (expensive at scale) or per-shard picks that cause duplicate/unstable ordering when resuming. We need an ergonomic API that: (1) is fast for common small-k use cases, (2) supports resumable pagination for larger explorations, (3) emits structured provenance and scoring metadata for downstream fairness/QA, and (4) scales horizontally without requiring full-candidate re-ranking on every page fetch.
background: Existing Linear tickets (see ENG-63210, ENG-36109) explored cursor and stable continuation concepts but either assumed a single reranker pass over all candidates or used opaque cursor designs that hid provenance. Our retrieval backend shards candidate sets; naive approaches either gather all candidates to a single re-ranker (expensive) or do independent per-shard top_k and merge with nondeterministic ties. Customers reported: (a) variable page ordering when documents tie on score, (b) high 95/99 latency for k>50, (c) difficulty debugging ranking regressions without per-item provenance.
proposal: Introduce a hybrid *shard-probe* + *global-rescore* flow with offset-based resumable pages and explicit provenance. Key ideas: 1) Probe: ask each retrieval shard for a lightweight 'probe' of T candidates (T configurable, default 2x requested page size) using cheap approximate scoring; 2) Merge & sample: locally merge probes, pick a merged candidate window and mark per-shard offsets; 3) Global rescore: run the full neural reranker only on the merged window; 4) Pagination & resume: return results and an opaque offset resume token that contains per-shard offsets + last-seen stable tiebreak (doc_id) + snapshot_id; 5) Determinism: stable tie-breaking rule (score desc, rerank_score desc, doc_id asc) to ensure deterministic order across pages; 6) Structured output: per-candidate fields {candidate_id, shard_id, probe_score, rerank_score, original_rank, provenance_tags}; 7) Streaming partials: support streaming early reranked candidates to reduce tail latency for first N items while later items compute in background. API surface includes parameters: page_size, resume_token, probe_factor, strict_top_k (bool), snapshot_id (optional).
api_contract: Request params: query, page_size (int), resume_token (string|null), probe_factor (float, default 2.0), strict_top_k (bool, default false), snapshot_id (string|null), explain (bool). Response: items: list of bundles; resume_token: opaque string; snapshot_id: string. Each item bundle fields returned as structured output strings: candidate_id, shard_id, probe_score, rerank_score, rank_position, provenance_keys (comma-separated), distance_metric, token_span_preview. Resume token format (opaque base64) encodes: request_id, per_shard_offsets (comma list), last_doc_id, snapshot_id, integrity_hash. The token is intentionally opaque to clients but small enough to fit in typical URLs. Backwards compatibility: if resume_token is absent and page_size<=50, backend uses probe_factor to minimize work and provide low latency. strict_top_k=true forces larger probes to guarantee exact global top-k at higher cost.
acceptance_criteria: API defined and documented in Console and public API docs (open spec + examples)
Server implements probe->merge->rescore flow behind feature flag 'rerank_v2'
Resume tokens round-trip: same token leads to same subsequent page ordering (deterministic) across 3k randomized tests
P50 latency for k<=10 under mixed traffic (1000 qps sim) < 100ms; P95 < 250ms for staged dataset
Cost delta: median CPU/GPU cycles per request < 1.4x vs current small-k baseline for probe_factor=2
Structured output includes per-item provenance fields and passes schema validation for all clients
tradeoffs_and_risks: Trade-offs: probe_factor reduces cost but may miss true global top-k unless strict_top_k is set. Resume tokens grow linearly with number of shards (we compress offsets; practical worst-case ~256 bytes). Snapshot_id required for strongly consistent corpora; for live indexes we document eventual-consistency caveats. Complexity increases in serving layer: maintaining probe path + resumable offsets and streaming partials requires changes across retrieval sharding, reranker batching, and request routing. Risk: exposing too much provenance could leak internal shard topology — we will obfuscate shard identifiers in public responses.
tasks: Design: finalize token binary layout and base64 encoding (Carlos)
Backend: implement probe API in retrieval layer with probe_factor support (eng-retrieval team)
Reranker: add batched rescore on merged windows and streaming partials (eng-rerank)
API: implement resume token handling, strict_top_k switching, snapshot plumbing (eng-api)
Console: docs and example snippets; update SDKs to decode explain field (dx)
E2E tests: determinism fuzz tests, large-scale load tests (perf infra)
Security review: obfuscation check for shard identifiers and token HMAC (security)
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout and internal dogfood, followed by opt-in beta customers
rollout_plan: Phase 0: API + backend behind 'rerank_v2' feature flag; internal unit tests and API contract review (1 week)
Phase 1: Dogfood in internal org with synthetic 1k qps load generator and real corpora (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Invite 2-3 beta customers, collect metrics and support feedback, iterate on token size and probe_factor defaults (3 weeks)
Phase 3: GA, defaulting probe_factor=2 for small-k and exposing strict_top_k opt-in; publish migration guide and SDK helpers (2 weeks)
notes: Design review 2026-03-05: PM agreed on snapshot_id approach; consensus to make resume_token opaque rather than JSON to avoid brittle client parsing.
Perf baseline runs 2026-03-08: initial probe_factor=2 reduced average reranker calls per request by ~60% on a 10-shard cluster for k=10 workloads.
Security flagged token integrity: will sign resume tokens with request-scoped HMAC and rotate keys quarterly.
UX decision: show 'partial' boolean on streamed responses so clients can wait for final=false before showing stable results in UI.
updates: 2026-03-03: Prototyped probe implementation; found an edge-case where identical doc_ids across shards broke tie rule; resolved by injecting stable global id mapping.
2026-03-06: Added snapshot_id to token to enable consistent paging in mutating corpora; backend will capture index snapshot at request start for beta customers.
2026-03-09: Benchmarks show P95 tail for k=50 reduced by 28% compared to naive global re-rank, system memory overhead increased by ~8% due to merged window buffers.
2026-03-10: PRs opened for retrieval and reranker; security review scheduled 2026-03-12.
